answer: At the jetty registry, each identity claims a karst survey route and posts a 60-credit pearl bond. No route may share a segment with an earlier route: the auditor checks overlap on the registry, and any overlap burns the bond. Survey cost rises as short routes go first: the k-th route costs 10 plus 2 per earlier route; the 1000th costs 2008. One thousand fakes spend 1,009,000 on surveys and lock 60,000 in bonds; one honest agent pays one 10 survey and recovers its bond. A route-rental ring fails: a rented survey repeats segments the registry holds, triggering the burn.
